obtaining thing at present hoped for

claims: If a man shall have thing hoped for

label: Hope from Prince/Nobleman, aspect application and ease/difficulty
claims: A separate method is introduced for the hope question.
The branch further refines conditions, not a reported new patient.
The request may concern something expected from a superior, patron or nobleman.
The source gives a dignity or advancement as an example.
Not every Eleventh House question implies employment.
The eleventh ruler applying to first ruler is favorable.
With either application the author says the applicant gets the requested item.
If the application is by trine or sextile the outcome is easier.
Trine/sextile signifies quick and comparatively easy attainment.
Ease and time are distinct from whether result happens.
A square or opposition is treated as laborious.
A negative aspect does not necessarily mean failure.
Lilly predicts obtaining the thing through considerable effort and delay.
He says the laborious meaning can hold even when the significators receive each other.
Reception does not automatically override every adverse aspect.
